the verb cluster in Dutch and German can be analysed without introducing a verbalcomplex and that the word order constraints on the German and Dutch verb cluster can be stated in terms of linear precedence statements only. van de Koot, M. (2000).

(i) the verb cluster in both German and Dutch can be accounted for by means of a single, general, HEAD-COMPLEMENT phrase structure schema, (ii) the verb cluster is not a phrase in its own right, but is part of a VP, and (iii) a single set of ordering constraints accounts for all ordering options in the verb clusters of both German and Dutch.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the question whether the verb cluster in Dutch and German can be analysed in a uniform way without resorting to a complex set of phrase structure rules, and without the introduction of additional phrase structure nodes.
the question whether the analysis of German and Dutch verb clustering can be based on the assumption that phrase structure imposes no ordering constraints on the elements of a verbal complex.
the question of whether a single set of constraints can account for the word order of verb clusters in German as well as in Dutch.

the present analysis is an improved version of the one presented in Van Noord and Bouman (1996) and that it is also an improvement on the earlier analysis in Hinrichs & Nakazawa (1994).

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that the analysis of Hinichs and Nakazawais not only an improvement on previous analyses in terms of the amount of data covered, but that the proposed approach is also more general and less ad hoc.
the Dutch and German verb clusters are similar, but not identical, and that the analysis of Hinrchs andNakazaawa (1989,1994) can be improved by adopting the ‘flat VP’ approach.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the verb clusters of German and Dutch can be analysed using the same set of constraints.
it is possible to account for the full range of verb clusters in German without introducing a verbalcomplex or any other special structure for the German and Dutch verb cluster.
the word order in German and Dutch can be accounted for in one and the same way.
